relevance_reason: Reports novel RAD21 mutations (intragenic exon 13 deletion, inherited from the mother, and a frameshift duplication) in two patients with atypical or mild CdLS.

findings.statement: Minor et al. (2014) reported 2 patients with atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome and RAD21 mutations. The first patient had developmental delay, hypospadias, inguinal hernia, and dysmorphic features. The second patient had developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and foot anomalies. The first patient was more mildly affected than the second.
quotes: The first patient presented with developmental delay, hypospadias, inguinal hernia and dysmorphic features while, the second patient presented with developmental delay, characteristic facial features, hirsutism, and hand and feet anomalies, with the first patient being milder than the second.

findings.statement: In a patient with mild atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome, Minor et al. (2014) identified an in-frame intragenic deletion of exon 13 of the RAD21 gene. The deletion was inherited from the patient's mother, who had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems. The authors described this as the first familial case.
quotes: One patient had an in-frame deletion of exon 13
The in-frame deletion mutation was found to be inherited from the mother who had a history of melanoma and other unspecified medical problems.

findings.statement: In a patient with atypical Cornelia de Lange syndrome, Minor et al. (2014) identified a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation in the RAD21 gene.
quotes: the second patient had a c.592_593dup frameshift mutation

findings.statement: Minor et al. (2014) discussed variable clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of RAD21 mutations. They emphasized the clinical utility of RAD21 mutation analysis in patients with atypical forms of CdLS, as well as molecular genetic testing in mildly affected patients.
quotes: This study expands the spectrum of RAD21 mutations and emphasizes the clinical utility of performing RAD21 mutation analysis in patients presenting with atypical forms of CdLS.
the variability of clinical presentation within families and low penetrance of mutations as well as the significance of performing molecular genetic testing in mildly affected patients are discussed.

relevance_reason: The abstract reports holoprosencephaly in people with variants in cohesin genes, including RAD21. This supports the midline brain defect part of CDLS4. The abstract gives no RAD21-specific variants or counts.

findings.statement: Kruszka et al. (2019) reported 4 individuals with holoprosencephaly who had variants in the non-X-linked cohesin complex genes SMC3 and RAD21. They also reported variants in the X-linked cohesin genes STAG2 and SMC1A in 11 other individuals with holoprosencephaly. The authors concluded that the cohesin complex is an important regulator of median forebrain development.
quotes: Additionally, we report four individuals with variants in the cohesin complex genes that are not X-linked, SMC3 and RAD21.
These findings show the cohesin complex as an important regulator of median forebrain development and X-linked inheritance patterns in holoprosencephaly.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with CdLS type 4 and a novel de novo RAD21 variant with structural modeling.

findings.statement: Gudmundsson et al. (2019) reported a 15-month-old boy with developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads, and diaphragmatic hernia, which the authors concluded expanded the clinical description of CdLS type 4.
quotes: We report a 15-month-old boy presenting with developmental delay, distinct CdLS-like facial features, gastrointestinal reflux in early infancy, testis retention, prominent digit pads and diaphragmatic hernia.

findings.statement: In a 15-month-old boy with CdLS type 4, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) identified by exome sequencing a de novo heterozygous 3-bp deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.1774_1776del), resulting in deletion of gln592 (p.Gln592del); the variant was absent from both healthy parents and was predicted to be disease-causing. In silico structural modeling predicted that the deletion disrupts contact between RAD21 lys591 and SMC1A residues glu1191 and glu1192, altering the RAD21-SMC1A interface.
quotes: Exome sequencing revealed a novel RAD21 variant, c.1774_1776del, p.(Gln592del), suggestive of CdLS type 4.
Segregation analysis of the two healthy parents confirmed the variant as de novo and bioinformatic analysis predicted the variant as disease-causing.

Assessment by in silico structural model predicted that the p.Gln592del variant results in a discontinued contact between RAD21-Lys591 and the SMC1A residues Glu1191 and Glu1192, causing changes in the RAD21-SMC1A interface.

relevance_reason: Largest case series of individuals with RAD21 variants (49 individuals, 33 families), with clinical delineation of RAD21-related CdLS, variant spectrum, protein modeling of missense variants, and genotype-phenotype analysis.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations (24 different intragenic sequence variants and 7 unique microdeletions), including 24 previously unpublished cases, from Australia, Europe, Turkey, Canada and the United States. Full clinical information was available for 29 individuals from 22 families (cohort A). All of them had CdLS clinical scores of at least 5. Their phenotype was an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared with that caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, with milder facial morphology, limb anomalies, cognition and behavior.
quotes: We gathered a series of 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations [24 different intragenic sequence variants (2 recurrent), 7 unique microdeletions], including 24 hitherto unpublished cases.
Their phenotype is an attenuated CdLS phenotype compared to that caused by variants in NIPBL or SMC1A for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially for cognition and behavior.
All patients in cohort A (age range 0–61 years, median 9 years, mean 18 years; 15 males) had CdLS scores of at least five, sufficient to warrant molecular genetic testing for CdLS.
findings.population: Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom, United States

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that in the 29 cohort A patients with RAD21 variants, the frequent features were short nose (23/26), long and/or smooth philtrum (26/29), concave nasal ridge (24/29), thick eyebrows (20/24), long eyelashes (21/26), synophrys (19/28), thin upper lip vermilion (23/29), short fifth finger (23/28), postnatal microcephaly (16/28) and gastroesophageal reflux (13/25). No patient had major limb malformations (0/29) or visual impairment (0/24). Small hands (5/27), small feet (3/27), hirsutism (10/26) and seizures (2/22) were less common than in the NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts. Hearing loss was present in 8/24, heart defects in 9/23 and cleft palate in 6/25.
quotes: Postnatal head circumference < − 2SD | HP:0000252 | 16/28 | 57 | 23/36 | 64 | 54/62 | 87
RAD21 patients less frequently have increased body hair (hirsutism, bushy eyebrows, low scalp hair lines), major limb malformations are not reported, and hands and feet are generally of normal size.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found that cognitive functioning and behavior were attenuated in RAD21 patients: 16 of 29 (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognition, none had severe or profound disability, and all patients aged 3 years and older used some words. Problems were mainly language-based. Behavioral problems were present in 14 of 25 (56%), mainly anxiety, ADHD, autistic features and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Self-injurious behavior (1/18) and aggression (1/16) were infrequent.
quotes: The majority of RAD21 patients (16/29, 55%) have normal or mildly impaired cognitive functioning (SMC1A group 32%; NIPBL group 7%)
Still, all RAD21 patients aged 3 years and above were able to use some words.
14/25 RAD21 patients (56%) with sufficiently available information on behavior had problems, mainly features of anxiety, ADHD, ASD, and obsessive–compulsive behavior.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported that in RAD21 patients pregnancies and births were usually normal and prenatal growth retardation was uncommon. Short stature and microcephaly developed after birth. About half had congenital anomalies such as cleft palate and cardiac anomalies. Unusual findings included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia or choanal atresia occurred occasionally.
quotes: The natural history data from the present study indicate that pregnancies and birth tend to progress normally, prenatal growth retardation being present in a small minority. About half of the patients have congenital anomalies (cleft palate; cardiac anomalies).
Unusual anomalies in the RAD21 cases are vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae).
Malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut are relatively frequent in RAD21 patients and have only rarely been described in CdLS

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) suggested, from limited data on cohort B, that biallelic RAD21 variants can cause Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants can cause holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics. In several further cases, including cases with sclerocornea, it was uncertain whether the RAD21 variant was involved.
quotes: In the 20 individuals with limited clinical information, additional phenotypes include Mungan syndrome (in patients with biallelic variants) and holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics.

The (limited) available information of individuals from cohort B suggests that biallelic RAD21 variants can also lead to Mungan syndrome and monoallelic RAD21 variants to holoprosencephaly (like one case in cohort A) and possibly schizophrenia

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found 31 different RAD21 alterations in 33 families: 7 unique deletions (6 of which also included other genes) and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Of the sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift) and were scattered throughout the gene, 3 were in-frame deletions, and the missense variants tended to cluster at the protein-binding domains. Two variants were recurrent (p.Cys585Arg and p.Arg586*). Nine of 21 index cases with known inheritance had familial variants.
quotes: The 33 families harbor 31 different variants: seven unique copy number variations (CNVs) and 24 intragenic sequence variants.
A relatively large proportion of the cases are familial (nine out of 21 index cases for whom inheritance could be established).
Of the 24 different sequence variants, 13 are predicted be truncating (2 nonsense, 2 splice site and 9 frameshift variants), and these are scattered throughout the gene.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 missense variant, c.1753T>C (p.Cys585Arg), in 2 families: it arose de novo in 1 previously reported patient and was found in 2 relatives in a new family. Molecular dynamics modeling predicted that Cys585Arg destabilizes the RAD21-SMC1A domain by causing the adjacent Arg586 to lose its salt-bridge contact with Glu577.
quotes: F13 | Deardorff 2012, P6 | Orginal data | ≥ 12 | Exon 14 | c.1753T > C | p.(Cys585Arg) | Missenseb | De novo
Cys585Arg has a similar effect, interacting with Glu583 and causing Arg586 to lose its contact with Glu577.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported a recurrent RAD21 nonsense variant, c.1756C>T (p.Arg586*), in 2 previously unpublished families. In one family it was inherited from the father, who was also affected. Facial morphology varied between the families carrying this variant.
quotes: F16a | Unpublished | New | 10 | Exon 14 | c.1756C > T | p.(Arg586*) | Nonsense | Familial (paternal)
Interfamilial variability is illustrated by the comparison of facial morphology between patients F15 and F16a/b who harbor the p.(Arg586*) variant.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) updated a family with a 1-bp deletion in RAD21, c.704delG (p.Ser235Ilefs*19), carried by 5 affected members, with CdLS scores of 9 to 12. Facial morphology varied within the family.
quotes: F6a | Boyle 2017 IV.16 | Updated | 12 | Exon 7 | c.704delG | p.(Ser235Ilefs*19) | Frameshift | Familial (maternal)
Intrafamilial variability is illustrated by the comparison of facial morphology between the members of family F6 and of family F16.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo in-frame deletion in RAD21, c.1774_1776del (p.Gln592del), in a previously reported patient with a CdLS score of 8. Molecular dynamics simulation predicted that loss of Gln592 distorts an alpha helix and moves Lys605 away from ATPase site 1 of the SMC1A/SMC3 head, disturbing the cohesin cycle.
quotes: F17 | Gudmunsson 2019 | Updated | 8 | Exon 14 | c.1774_1776del | p.(Gln592del) | Inframe deletionb | De novo
This situation promotes a conformational change in the alpha helix, causing the Lys605, which is placed in the same alpha helix, to move away from site 1 of the ATPase.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a RAD21 in-frame deletion, c.1800_1802del (p.Phe600del), in a previously unpublished patient with classic CdLS who had no variants in other known CdLS genes on a targeted gene panel. Modeling did not show a structural effect, but the authors considered the variant likely pathogenic based on the phenotype.
quotes: F18 | Unpublished | New | 9 | Exon 14 | c.1800_1802del | p.(Phe600del) | Inframe deletionb |

Although the Phe600del variant does not seem to affect RAD21 structure, it leads to a classical CdLS phenotype without variants in additional known CdLS genes (using a targeted gene panel). Thus, it does seem likely pathogenic.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1808T>C (p.Leu603Pro), in a previously reported patient in cohort B. Modeling predicted that Pro603 bends the alpha helix and moves Lys605 out of its position near ATPase site 1.
quotes: F29 | Lee 2014 P76 | Original data | | Exon 14 | c.1808T > C | p.(Leu603Pro) | Missenseb | De novo

Presence of mutated Pro603 instead of wild-type Leu603 promotes a local change in the bending angle of the alpha-helix in which it is located, resulting in a conformational change in the alpha helix that moves Lys605 out of its initial position close to ATPase site 1

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) found a de novo RAD21 missense variant, c.1033T>C (p.Ser345Pro), in a DECIPHER patient. Modeling predicted that it impairs the interaction between RAD21 and STAG1/2 by creating a new curved alpha-helix segment that separates from the STAG2 surface. The previously reported de novo variant c.1127C>G (p.Pro376Arg) was predicted to form a new salt bridge that over-stabilizes the RAD21-STAG2 interaction.
quotes: F26 | Decipher 275402 | New | | Exon 9 | c.1033T > C | p.(Ser345Pro) | Missenseb | De novo

The Ser345Pro variant impairs RAD21 and STAG1/2 interactions due to promotion of a de novo curved small alpha-helix segment that binds to the pre-existing alpha helix, which separates from the surface of STAG2.
Nevertheless, Pro376Arg does promote the formation of a new salt bridge between RAD21 and STAG2, which is predicted to cause over-stabilization of the interaction between the two proteins.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) updated the family with Mungan syndrome in which 3 sibs were homozygous for the RAD21 variant c.1864G>A (p.Ala622Thr). Modeling showed no structural alteration. However, Ala622 lies next to Thr623, a PLK1 phosphorylation site, and earlier zebrafish morpholino studies supported pathogenicity. Heterozygous family members had some CdLS-spectrum features, but it remained uncertain whether the heterozygous variant causes a phenotype.
quotes: F30a | Bonora 2015 IV.9 | Updated | | Exon 14 | c.[1864G > A];[1864G > A] | p.(Ala622Thr) | Missenseb | Familial (both parents)

The heterozygous members of this family had some clinical features of the CdLS spectrum, but as it was not possible to retrieve further clinical data, it remains uncertain whether they have a full CdLS phenotype, and whether this variant can lead to a phenotype in heterozygous form.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported further previously unpublished heterozygous RAD21 variants in CdLS patients. These were a de novo frameshift c.617_620del (p.Ile206Thrfs*3), a de novo frameshift c.1635del (p.Gly547Alafs*65), a paternally inherited missense variant c.1382C>T (p.Thr461Ile), and a missense variant c.194G>A (p.Arg65Gln) from ClinVar that was reported as a VUS. Based on phenotype, modeling and the literature, the authors considered Arg65Gln and Thr461Ile likely pathogenic, possibly through altered phosphorylation motifs or PDS5 interaction.
quotes: F5 | Unpublished | New | 9 | Exon 6 | c.617_620del | p.(Ile206Thrfs*3) | Frameshift | De novo
F12 | Unpublished | New | 13 | Exon 13 | c.1635del | p.(Gly547Alafs*65) | Frameshift | De novo
F10 | Unpublished | New | 10 | Exon 11 | c.1382C > T | p.(Thr461Ile) | Missense | Familial (paternal)

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) observed a trend toward higher CdLS scores and more frequent growth impairment in patients with microdeletions than in those with intragenic variants, but no difference in major malformations or in cognitive and behavioral problems. CdLS scores did not differ between truncating and nontruncating sequence variants. Variability within and between families was striking, especially in cognition and behavior, and in most families it could not be explained by mosaicism.
quotes: There was a trend towards higher CdLS scores and more frequently impaired growth parameters in patients with microdeletions compared to those with intragenic variants, but no differences were apparent in frequency of major malformations or cognitive and behavioral problems.

There was no difference in CdLS scores or growth parameters between individuals with truncating and those with non-truncating sequence variants (median 10; range 9–13 and median 9.5; range 5–12, respectively).
The intrafamilial variation cannot be explained by mosaicism in most families.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) noted that RAD21 variants were frequently familial (familial in 5 of 12 cohort A cases with known inheritance). Mildly affected parents were sometimes diagnosed only after more severely affected offspring were recognized, so the authors recommended parental testing even when parents appear unaffected.
quotes: Not uncommonly, RAD21 patients are able to start a family, and some are only diagnosed when more severely affected offspring is recognized.
Parental testing is warranted, even if signs or symptoms are apparently absent in parents, and standard testing of parents may further broaden the phenotype of RAD21 variants.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) suggested that the relatively mild phenotype indicates RAD21 is not highly intolerant to loss of function, unlike other CdLS genes. They speculated that RAD21 haploinsufficiency may be compensated more effectively than loss of other cohesin genes, noting that haploinsufficiency gave roughly halved RAD21 RNA without compensatory upregulation.
quotes: The relatively mild phenotype of patients with RAD21 variants seems to indicate that RAD21 is not highly intolerant to loss-of-function, in contrast to other CdLS-associated genes (NIPBL, SMC1A, PDS5, WAPL, STAG2)
One may speculate that the effect of haploinsufficiency of RAD21 on the function of the cohesin ring can be compensated more effectively compared to the other cohesin genes.

findings.statement: Krab et al. (2020) reported that no RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular testing. CdLS had been suspected before testing in about 60% of index cases (13/21). The authors concluded that the CdLS score remains a reliable tool.
quotes: In about 60% of index cases (13/21 index cases in which this was specified) CdLS was suspected prior to testing.
No RAD21 variant would have been missed using the CdLS consensus criteria for molecular studies (Kline et al. 2018).

relevance_reason: Revises the diagnosis of a previously reported girl with an 8q23.3q24.13 deletion including RAD21 to CDLS4.

findings.statement: Pereza et al. (2015) revised their earlier diagnosis of Langer-Giedion syndrome in a girl with a 7.5-Mb interstitial deletion at 8q23.3q24.13. The deletion included EXT1 but not TRPS1. Because it also included RAD21 and 30 other RefSeq genes, the authors suggested that the correct diagnosis was Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4. They compared her with other reported patients who had CDLS4 caused by heterozygous 8q24 deletions.
quotes: we reported on a girl with Langer-Giedion syndrome (LGS) phenotype and a 7.5 Mb interstitial deletion at 8q23.3q24.13, encompassing the EXT1, but not the TRPS1 gene
Considering that the interstitial deletion in our patient included the RAD21 and 30 other RefSeq genes, we would like to suggest a revision of the diagnosis reported in our previous paper

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with features of CdLS4 plus Langer-Giedion syndrome caused by a germline chromothripsis deletion that includes RAD21 and EXT1. RAD21 expression was reduced in the patient's cells. This is a contiguous gene deletion case that adds evidence on the RAD21 haploinsufficiency phenotype.

findings.statement: Lei et al. (2020) described a 6-year-old Han Chinese boy, the first child of healthy unrelated parents, who had a de novo t(8;18)(q22;q21) translocation. He had growth retardation (height and weight -2.0 SD), mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, left-sided cleft palate, and a congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle, and juxtaposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery). He also had thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebrae, fifth-finger clinodactyly, fingerpads, umbilical and inguinal hernias, recurrent respiratory infections, and facial dysmorphism including arched thick eyebrows, long eyelashes, a depressed nasal bridge, anteverted nostrils, large prominent ears, dental malocclusion, and micrognathia. Kabuki syndrome was initially suspected, and multiple exostoses were found at age 10 years.
quotes: He was the first child of healthy, unrelated parents of Han-Chinese origin with unremarkable family history, with a karyotype of 46,XY,t(8;18)(q22;q21)dn (Fig. 1a).

He had mild-to-moderate ID, congenital heart defect (ventricular septal defect, right ventricle double exit, aorta, and pulmonary artery juxtaposition), thoracic scoliosis, butterfly vertebra (T5, T8, T10, and T12), clinodactyly of fifth fingers, fingerpads, umbilical hernia (left side), inguinal hernia, recurrent respiratory infections
He was found to have multiple exostoses in his right leg, left calf and shoulder blade at the age of 10 years.

findings.statement: Lei et al. (2020) used nanopore long-read sequencing and the dnarrange pipeline in this patient. The de novo t(8;18) translocation turned out to be germline chromothripsis: the genome had been shattered into 19 fragments (15 from chromosome 8 and 4 from chromosome 18) that rejoined in random order and orientation. The rearrangement caused 4 deletions on chromosome 8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3,529 kb) and 1 deletion on chromosome 18 (1,528 kb), all of which were consistent with array results. One chromosome 8 deletion contained RAD21 and EXT1 but not TRPS1. Earlier short-read whole-genome sequencing had not resolved the rearrangement, and no pathogenic variants were found in the Kabuki syndrome genes.
quotes: The patient genome was evidently shattered into 19 fragments, and rejoined into derivative chromosomes in a random order and orientation.
The rearrangement involves four large deletions from chr8 (456, 1,957, 520, and 3529 kb) and one large deletion from chr18 (1528 kb) (Fig. 2b, yellow rectangles).
We noted that one deletion from chr8 contained disease associated genes, RAD21 and EXT1 (Figs. 3a, S4).

findings.statement: Lei et al. (2020) found reduced RAD21 and EXT1 expression on quantitative RT-PCR of the patient's lymphoblastoid cells, while TRPS1 expression was unchanged. They concluded that loss of RAD21 and EXT1 explained the phenotype, a likely contiguous gene syndrome combining CdLS4 and atypical Langer-Giedion syndrome. They considered involvement of other disrupted genes, including ZFPM2, unlikely.
quotes: Real-time PCR results from the LCLs of the patient showed decreased gene expression of RAD21 (OMIM 606462) and EXT1 (OMIM 608177) but not TRPS1 (OMIM 604386) (Fig. 3b, Table S5).

These two genes could fully explain the disease phenotype with facial dysmorphisms and bone abnormality, which is likely a contiguous gene syndrome, Cornelia de Lange syndrome type IV (CdLs-4) and atypical Langer-Giedion syndrome (LGS), also known as trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type II (TRPSII).

findings.statement: Lei et al. (2020) compared their patient with 5 previously reported patients who had Langer-Giedion syndrome with deletions that included RAD21 and EXT1 but spared TRPS1. The 6 patients shared overlapping features: arched thick eyebrows (6 patients), long eyelashes (5), depressed or broad nasal bridge (5), sparse scalp hair (4), and intellectual disability (4 of 6). Only their patient had thoracic scoliosis and a congenital heart defect. Because 2 of 8 previously reported patients with RAD21 variants had congenital heart disease, the authors suggested that RAD21 deficiency might be responsible for the heart disease.
quotes: Interestingly, five patients with Langer–Giedion syndrome without TRPS1 gene disruption have been reported (Fig. 3a). Consistent with our patient, all five patients have deletions involving RAD21 and EXT1.
In addition to these symptoms, our patient had thoracic scoliosis and congenital heart defect, which were not described in the five patients previously reported.
It is possible that RAD21 defect might be responsible for this patient’s congenital heart disease.

relevance_reason: This is the original report linking RAD21 mutations to a Cornelia de Lange-like cohesinopathy (CDLS4).

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) reported that children with RAD21 mutations had growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlapped those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS). Unlike children with mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3, these individuals had much milder cognitive impairment than those with classic CdLS.
quotes: Children with RAD21 mutations display growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap findings in individuals with CdLS.
Notably, unlike children with mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3, these individuals have much milder cognitive impairment than those with classical CdLS.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) showed that human mutations in RAD21, an integral structural protein of the cohesin complex, cause a congenital phenotype consistent with a cohesinopathy. They suggested that dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and worse structural and cognitive clinical findings than loss-of-function mutations.
quotes: Here we show that human mutations in the integral cohesin structural protein RAD21 result in a congenital phenotype consistent with a "cohesinopathy."
Our data suggest that, compared to loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and cause worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) suggested that, compared to RAD21 loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations cause more severe functional defects and worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.
quotes: Our data suggest that, compared to loss-of-function mutations, dominant missense mutations result in more severe functional defects and cause worse structural and cognitive clinical findings.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) found that the RAD21 mutations act at the interface between RAD21 and the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, and that they impair the cellular DNA damage response.
quotes: Mechanistically, these mutations act at the RAD21 interface with the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, impair cellular DNA damage response, and disrupt transcription in a zebrafish model.

findings.statement: Deardorff et al. (2012) showed in a zebrafish model that the RAD21 mutations disrupted transcription.
quotes: Mechanistically, these mutations act at the RAD21 interface with the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A, impair cellular DNA damage response, and disrupt transcription in a zebrafish model.

relevance_reason: Reports a novel RAD21 frameshift variant in a family with CdLS showing intrafamilial variability and incomplete penetrance.

findings.statement: In a patient with Cornelia de Lange syndrome (individual IV.16), Boyle et al. (2017) identified a novel heterozygous 1-bp deletion (c.704delG) in the RAD21 gene, predicted to result in a frameshift and premature stop codon (p.Ser235IlefsTer19) with a deleterious effect. The deletion was also found in the patient's mother and 2 aunts, none of whom had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy before the study.
quotes: In a patient with CdLS (IV.16) we identifed a novel single basepair deletion (c.704delG) in RAD21, which encodes a cohesin pathway protein.
The variant is predicted to result in a premature stop codon [p.(Ser235Ilefs*19)] and hereby would have a deleterious effect.
Notably, the deletion was found in the mother and the two aunts of the index patient, and none of them had been suspected of having CdLS or a cohesinopathy prior to this study (a).

findings.statement: Boyle et al. (2017) reported intrafamilial phenotypic variation in a family segregating a RAD21 deletion: the index patient could be classified as having mild CdLS, whereas the mother and 2 aunts carrying the variant did not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for CdLS. The authors suggested that, together with previous reports, this indicates incomplete penetrance associated with RAD21 variants and that such individuals may be underdiagnosed.
quotes: The index patient can be classified as mild CdLS, but the other family members do not fulfill the diagnostic criteria of CdLS.
This study together with previous reports suggests incomplete penetrance associated with RAD21 variants and these individuals may therefore be underdiagnosed.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It is a reply to a correspondence about another case of holoprosencephaly linked to a RAD21 loss-of-function variant, which relates directly to the midline brain defect part of CDLS4. The title gives no patient or variant details.

findings.statement: Kruszka (2020) replied to a correspondence that reported another case of holoprosencephaly associated with a RAD21 loss-of-function variant.
quotes: Reply: Another case of holoprosencephaly associated with RAD21 loss-of-function variant.

relevance_reason: The title reports a patient with holoprosencephaly and a RAD21 loss-of-function variant, which bears directly on CDLS4 with midline brain defects. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Goel and Parasivam (2020) reported another case of holoprosencephaly associated with a loss-of-function variant in the RAD21 gene.
quotes: Another case of holoprosencephaly associated with RAD21 loss-of-function variant.

relevance_reason: Case report of a new patient with a RAD21 intragenic mutation and mild CdLS. It adds a further case to CDLS4, but the abstract gives no details about the variant.

findings.statement: Dorval et al. (2020) reported a boy with a mild Cornelia de Lange syndrome presentation and a molecularly confirmed novel RAD21 mutation. They compared his clinical features with those of previously described patients carrying different RAD21 intragenic mutations to further delineate the phenotype. They noted that RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype.
quotes: A novel RAD21 mutation in a boy with mild Cornelia de Lange presentation: Further delineation of the phenotype.
We discuss a new patient with RAD21 confirmed molecular diagnosis and compare his clinical features to those of previously described patients carrying different RAD21 intragenic mutations.
Among them, RAD21 is associated with a milder phenotype.

relevance_reason: The abstract describes a boy with a de novo 8q24 interstitial deletion that includes EXT1 and genes distal to it, with multiple exostoses, intellectual disability, hypertrichosis and epilepsy. The abstract does not mention RAD21 or Cornelia de Lange syndrome, so it is useful only as context on contiguous deletions in the region.

findings.statement: Wuyts et al. (2002) described a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy, along with brain abnormalities, caused by a de novo submicroscopic interstitial deletion of chromosome 8q24. Molecular analysis showed that the deleted region overlapped the Langer-Giedion syndrome region and included the EXT1 gene and additional genes distal to EXT1. The deletion probably did not include the TRPS1 gene, which lies proximal to EXT1.
quotes: Here we describe a boy with multiple exostoses, hypertrichosis, mental retardation, and epilepsy due to a de novo deletion on chromosome 8q24.

Molecular analysis revealed that the deletion interval overlaps with the Langer-Giedion syndrome and involves the EXT1 gene and additional genes located distal to EXT1, but probably not encompassing the TRPS1 gene located proximal to EXT1.
